items.title: Kerr, Spoelstra, Lue Remain Atop List Of NBA’s Highest-Paid Coaches
items.summary: When Warriors head coach Steve Kerr signed a new two-year contract with the team in May, reporting indicated that he would remain the NBA’s highest-paid coach as a result of the deal. Kurt Badenhausen of Sportico confirms as much, writing that Kerr’s latest contract is in the same salary range as his previous one, at $17.5MM annually. Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra and Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue, who were tied for the second spot on Badenhausen’s list of the NBA’s highest-paid coaches a year ago, held their places this season, as both are on long-term deals worth an average of $15MM per year. items.summary: The Warriors, who are 7-2 when Stephen Curry plays a full game this season, beat Boston 88-87 on Sunday for their first victory since the star guard went down with an abdominal injury. items.title: Josh Hart Playing Through Shoulder Injury
items.summary: Knicks forward Josh Hart, who spoke last week about trying to “get right” physically, has dealt with calf and ankle problems this fall and is also playing through a finger issue that will likely require joint replacement surgery once his playing career is over. On top of all that, Hart acknowledged to Stefan Bondy of The New York Post (subscription required) that he’s battling a right shoulder injury too. “A lot of things are going on with my shoulder,” Hart told Bondy after he played a season-high 39 minutes and registered a triple-double in Sunday’s win over Indiana. “It’s been barking for a couple weeks. So now, we got a couple days where we can figure some stuff out within the couple-day break and hopefully get it feeling better.” Off days on Monday and Tuesday this week will give Hart a brief rest, but there’s no indication he plans to take any games off to let the shoulder heal.…

items.title: Bulls Waive Orlando Robinson
items.summary: The Bulls have placed big man Orlando Robinson on waivers, the team announced today (via Twitter). The move opens up a slot on Chicago’s 15-man roster, leaving the club with 14 players on standard contracts. Robinson’s minimum-salary deal, which he signed on November 13, was non-guaranteed, so the Bulls will only be on the hook for a prorated portion of his cap hit. Assuming he goes unclaimed on waivers, Robinson will earn $211,257, which is equivalent to 14 days’ worth of his minimum salary — he spent 11 days on Chicago’s roster and will be on waivers for three more. Robinson didn’t actually play for the Bulls at all during his time under contract. He was on the roster to provide emergency frontcourt depth and to ensure that Chicago was able to make the most of its two-way player availability, tweets K.C. Johnson of the Chicago Sports Network. When a team is carrying fewer than 15…

items.title: Nuggets’ Julian Strawther Cleared For Season Debut
items.summary: No players are listed on the Nuggets’ latest injury report (Twitter link), which means that Julian Strawther will be available for the first time this season when the Mavericks visit Denver on Tuesday. Strawther suffered a left knee injury during the Nuggets’ preseason game on October 14 and was diagnosed with a sprain two days left after undergoing imaging. The 6’6″ guard was ruled out for at least six weeks, but he’ll beat that projected timeline, having been cleared to make his season debut roughly five-and-a-half weeks after the team made that announcement. The 29th overall pick in the 2023 draft, Strawther appeared in 172 regular season games for Denver during his first three NBA seasons, averaging 7.1 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1.1 assists in 16.2 minutes per contest, with a .429/.346/.801 shooting line. items.title: Pacers Notes: Nesmith, McConnell, Smith, Shooting, More
items.summary: Small forward Aaron Nesmith converted 39.6% of his three-point attempts in his first four years with the Pacers, but he’s mired in a brutal slump to open his fifth season in Indiana. He has gone 0-for-13 from long distance over his last four games, dropping his three-point percentage to 26.3% through 15 appearances. Nesmith, who’s owed about $51.4MM over the next three seasons, will miss Monday’s game against Oklahoma City due to right foot soreness, Dustin Dopirak of The Indianapolis Star reports, noting that foot and ankle problems have plagued the 27-year-old for years (All Twitter links). Head coach Rick Carlisle said pregame that Nesmith is “banged up” with foot, ankle and knee injuries, Dopirak adds, but the team hopes he won’t be out long. items.summary: After a 4-3 start, the Wizards lost eight straight games, putting increased scrutiny on head coach Brian Keefe, as Josh Robbins and David Aldridge of The Athletic (free link) wrote last week. Veteran wing Khris Middleton helped organize a players-only meeting when the losing streak hit eight games and told his teammates to maintain communication, play more physically, and “show a little bit more fight,” according to fourth-year forward Bilal Coulibaly. items.title: Cameron Boozer Out At Least Four Weeks With Ankle Injury
items.summary: Rookie forward Cameron Boozer, the third overall pick in the 2026 draft, will miss at least four weeks after testing revealed a moderate-grade medial sprain of his right ankle, the Grizzlies announced (via Twitter). According to Michael Wallace of Grind City Media (Twitter link), Memphis is taking “extreme precaution” in its approach to Boozer’s injury, which occurred in the third quarter of Thursday’s win over Golden State. The former Duke star is traveling with the Grizzlies on their road trip, Wallace adds. It’s a tough blow for Boozer, an early contender for Rookie of the Year, and for the Grizzlies, who are already missing forwards GG Jackson II (foot fracture/surgery) and Jerami Grant (calf strain). Guard Scotty Pippen Jr. (herniated disc) remains sidelined as well. The Grizzlies have been ravaged by injuries over the past couple years, a trend that seems to be continuing in…

items.title: Bulls Notes: Splitter, Giddey, Buzelis, Hield, Smith
items.summary: The Bulls’ rocky season continued on Friday with a close loss to Washington in which starters Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis were benched for the final 7:59 of the fourth quarter. As Julia Poe of The Chicago Tribune writes, both players were once viewed as cornerstone pieces for the Bulls, but it’s no longer clear if that’s the case under a new front office led by Bryson Graham and a new head coach in Tiago Splitter. Splitter had a simple and incisive explanation for his decision afterward, telling reporters, “I thought they didn’t have a good game.” While Splitter has said he has no plans to remove either player from the starting five, it’s apparent neither is a lock to be part of closing lineups after multiple late-game benchings, Poe notes. items.title: Nikola Jokic, Anthony Davis Named Players Of The Week
items.summary: Nuggets center Nikola Jokic is the Western Conference Player of the Week, according to the NBA (Twitter link), with Wizards big man Anthony Davis claiming the award in the East. Jokic and Davis won for games played from Nov. 16 – 22 (Week 5 of the regular season). After a relatively slow start to the season by his lofty standards, three-time MVP Jokic averaged 28.8 points, 12.0 rebounds and 9.5 assists on .600/.421/.895 shooting last week. Denver went 3-1 in those games, with a loss to Phoenix followed by wins against Boston, Houston and Chicago. Davis helped Washington go 3-1 last week, including three straight wins that snapped an eight-game losing streak. The 10-time All-Star forward/center averaged 26.5 PPG, 9.0 RPG, 1.5 APG, 1.3 BPG and 1.0 SPG on .586/.444/.714 shooting in a loss to Memphis and wins over Toronto, Chicago and Orlando.
